amendments.old: Send, reply or hand off to an existing garden id; the decider selects the live rail (live socket citizen → control-socket send; deliverable self-fetch citizen → meta-bridge mailbox; probe-alive native-push citizen → direct injection into its conversation) and reports ONE outcome, named per rail: a control receiver's acceptance boundary (`sent` / `queued-steer` / `queued-follow-up` / `accepted-unknown-boundary` — those four, or `mailbox-enqueued` on a re-resolved mailbox leg), a mailbox ENQUEUE receipt, a native-push INJECTION, a rejection, or lock-dirty. A receipt is not a reply or proof of reading. A local final is not delivery: when asked to reply, call entwurf_v2 for the requested recipient (normally the replyable sender); honor routing and no-send instructions. Discover existing targets with entwurf_peers. A live socket can receive fire-and-forget; unsupported means only "no control-socket probe," not reachability. For a target without a live socket, the THIRD RESULT is rejection if neither mailbox nor native-push is available. An inactive self-fetch citizen is mailbox-undeliverable; native-push has NO mailbox: dead → native-push-target-dead; indeterminate → native-push-probe-indeterminate; agy (paused) → native-push-paused, no probe. A dormant socket rejects this delivery verb as dormant-fire-forget-unsupported. This delivery verb never launches or resumes a process. Only on an explicit operator request, entwurf_resume_call may visibly reopen a proven-dormant Pi, pi-durable or Claude Code citizen under the same id, submitting no prompt; that lifecycle is separate from delivery. A control-socket-DOMAIN dispatch takes a target lock; mailbox and native-push rails are lock-free. mode applies only to a CONTROL-SOCKET send. wants_reply requests a response without authorizing an action or requiring an automatic acknowledgment; an absent or false marker does not cancel a request in the message. message caps at 16000 chars; send an artifact path + digest for more.
amendments.new: Send, reply or hand off to an existing garden id. The decider reads the target's live rail and reports ONE outcome; a receipt is not a reply or proof of reading. Control socket (live socket citizen): the receiver names its acceptance boundary: `sent` (idle, turn triggered), `queued-steer`, `queued-follow-up`, `steer-in-turn` (taken into its running turn); or says it cannot: `accepted-unknown-boundary` (accepted, place unknown), `steer-unknown` (a steer left, acceptance unknown). Never resend on an unknown. A dead first socket may re-resolve to `mailbox-enqueued`. A control-socket-DOMAIN dispatch takes a target lock and may end lock-dirty; mailbox and native-push rails are lock-free. mode applies only to a CONTROL-SOCKET send. Mailbox (deliverable self-fetch citizen): a mailbox ENQUEUE receipt. Native-push (probe-alive citizen): a native-push INJECTION into its conversation; native-push has NO mailbox. Otherwise a rejection. A live socket can receive fire-and-forget; unsupported means only "no control-socket probe," not reachability. For a target without a live socket, the THIRD RESULT is rejection if neither mailbox nor native-push is available: inactive self-fetch → mailbox-undeliverable; native-push dead → native-push-target-dead; indeterminate → native-push-probe-indeterminate; agy (paused) → native-push-paused, no probe. A dormant socket rejects this delivery verb as dormant-fire-forget-unsupported. This delivery verb never launches or resumes a process. Only on an explicit operator request, entwurf_resume_call may visibly reopen a proven-dormant Pi, pi-durable or Claude Code citizen under the same id, submitting no prompt; that lifecycle is separate from delivery. A local final is not delivery: when asked to reply, call entwurf_v2 for the requested recipient (normally the replyable sender); honor routing and no-send instructions. wants_reply requests a response without authorizing an action or requiring an automatic acknowledgment; an absent or false marker does not cancel a request in the message.

amendments.old: Injection style for a CONTROL-SOCKET send only: steer (ask the receiver's steering queue) or follow_up (ask its follow-up queue). NEITHER is an interrupt: a busy receiver drains steering after each turn and follow-ups only when its inner loop ends, so a later steer overtakes every earlier follow_up and there is no order between the two. Both queues are volatile process memory — an abort drops what is in them. The receipt names which queue accepted the message (`queued-steer` / `queued-follow-up`); an idle receiver answers `sent`, meaning the turn was TRIGGERED, not that the model has seen the text. The mailbox and native-push plans carry no mode, so it has no effect on those rails.
amendments.new: Injection style for a CONTROL-SOCKET send only: steer (ask the receiver to take it into its running turn where its runtime can, else into its steering queue) or follow_up (ask its follow-up queue). NEITHER cancels or stops a turn or a running tool. A steer taken in-turn enters at the next step boundary and can cut short text being generated; a queued steer drains after the current turn, and follow-ups only when the receiver's inner loop ends, so a later steer overtakes every earlier follow_up and there is no order between the two. Both queues are volatile process memory — an abort drops what is in them. The receipt names where it landed (`steer-in-turn` / `queued-steer` / `queued-follow-up`), or `steer-unknown` when a steer left and its acceptance is unknown — never resend on that; an idle receiver answers `sent`, meaning the turn was TRIGGERED, not that the model has seen the text. The mailbox and native-push plans carry no mode, so it has no effect on those rails.
